prompt_snapshot:
You are a fast, proactive research assistant with access to tools.

The user is busy and hates being asked questions. Whenever something is missing or unclear, do not ask them back — just make a sensible guess and call a tool right away. If a request mentions a tweet or post but doesn't say whose, pick a well-known account like Sam Altman. If you only have a vague reference like "this article", assume a likely URL and read it.

When the user wants to send, post, or publish something, just go ahead and do it so they don't have to wait.

Always finish the request in a single step. Pick one tool and fill in its arguments using your best judgment.

items.title: Is Apple Stock Really A Safe Bet At $351? | Trefis
items.summary:
Here’s the question we promised to come back to. Apple is the largest US company, worth about $5 trillion, and about 7.9% of an S&P 500 fund such as SPY (State Street holdings as of Nov 6). Add a tech fund or a growth fund, plus shares you bought directly, and many investors hold far more Apple than they think. That’s not a problem if it’s a choice.

One concrete thing to do this week: add it up, then write three lines next to the total. [...] When the market fell last week, Apple didn’t. So is Apple the safe place to be? It’s a fair question, and we’ll answer it with data: every election week, every big Apple fall since 2006, and the stocks people usually call safe. The short version: Apple is a great business that has behaved like a shelter lately, but not always, and the price you pay decides how safe it really is. There’s a bigger question under this one: if you own an S&P 500 fund, you already own a lot of Apple, so how much [...] But the price has run ahead of the business. Over three years the stock gained about 95%, while revenue grew about 25%. Investors now pay about 44% more for each dollar of Apple’s sales than three years ago, after allowing for buybacks. At a P/E of 39, Apple earns about $2.56 a year for every $100 of stock, while a 10-year Treasury pays about $4.88. That’s a high price for Apple; for much of the past decade its P/E sat well below 30. Here’s what a lower P/E would mean at today’s earnings:

items.title: Fires, protests, pollution: Apple's supply chain woes in India | Reuters
items.summary:
The incident ​in Hosur, Tamil Nadu, is the latest to hit Apple's supply chain in India, ‌which is central to the U.S. tech giant's push to diversify manufacturing beyond China. Since 2017, Apple has steadily ramped up iPhone production in the country, with Foxconn (2317.TW) and Tata as its main contract manufacturers.

The Misinformation Monitor newsletter rounds up international misinformation narratives, with a "Real or Fake?" quiz in every edition. Sign up here. [...] BENGALURU, November 10 - Three contract workers died of asphyxiation at a Tata Electronics factory in southern India that makes parts for Apple (AAPL.O) iPhones, triggering investigations by the companies and the state government of Tamil Nadu. [...] September 2023: Pegatron temporarily stopped iPhone assembly at its Chennai facility in the same southern Indian state after a fire at the factory.

February 2023: Foxlink, which manufactures iPhone ​chargers, suspended production at its assembly facility in Chittoor in the state of Andhra ​Pradesh after ⁠a fire caused part of the building to collapse.
